long_biography.plain_text:
Seeing another operator advance cash against customers' postdated cheques prompted Allan Jones to test the model in Cleveland, Tennessee. He opened the first Check Into Cash store ten days later in 1993 with $10,000, then reinvested the business's earnings during its first decade. The result was a national short-term-lending chain that grew to more than 1,300 stores at its peak.

Jones's earlier experience came through his father's credit bureau, which he joined at 20, bought in 1977 and expanded before selling its reporting division to Equifax. Beyond lending, he used Jones Properties to restore downtown Cleveland buildings and later established the Allan Jones Foundation. Its support has ranged across education, health, historic preservation and environmental work, while his backing of local wrestling programs became one of his most visible community commitments.
